text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The U.S. State Department's annual country report for 1996 says the Zimbabwe government generally respects human rights but cites a number of violations.

- Medical practitioners affiliated to Harare's exclusive Avenue and Montage clinics have expressed reservations about the proposed sale of a 60 percent strategic shareholding in Medical Investments Ltd (MIL), which owns and manages two clinics, to South Africa's African Oxygen Ltd.
- The Zimbabwe Investment Centre said it was satisfied that work on sensitising local authorities on matters relating to attracting and retaining inward investment has worked.

- Zimbabwe's financial markets were currently a good investment, due to rapid growth of the industry. Financial awareness in the securities is a growing part of Zimbabwe business life, an official said.
- The success of the country's current economic reforms largely depends on the performance of the manufacturing industry, says the Confederation of Zimbabwe Industries.
- Rural bus fares go up by 15.5 percent with effect from February 21, which represents 21 cents per passenger a kilometre, up from 18 cents per single person for the same distance.
- Police traffic patrol and motorcycles will from Friday carry screening devices as the force intensifies attempts to reduce cases of drunken driving.
- The government is willing to allow local authorities to build and run secondary schools, education minister Gabriel Machinga said.
